title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are working notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture on a divided-power ('pd') de Rham complex for simplicial objects. Such a complex is a version of Sullivan-style polynomial forms that works over an arbitrary base ring k, using divided powers instead of rational coefficients. The faint typed text showing through is the reverse side of a typescript of SGA 7 Exp. IX (Barsotti-Tate groups, Prop. 9.5.6). It is unrelated to the handwritten mathematics, and so are the 'neighbouring page' transcriptions.

The page sets up a coefficient formalism, step by step.

(1) The 'line' data. Coefficient data is a quadruple (s, s^+, gamma, t):
- s is an algebra-like object playing the role of the affine line;
- s^+ is an augmentation ideal;
- gamma is a divided-power structure;
- t is a 'coordinate'.
From this a functor A_*(s, s^+, gamma, t) of 'simplicial forms' is built.

(2) The standard choice. Take s = k[[u]] (or k[u]) with s^+ = (u), and canonical divided-power coordinates on k[[u]]^+ and s^+. These correspond to the coordinates on k'{{T}}^+, the divided-power (series) algebra in T over a k-algebra k'. The coordinate t is defined as a linear form on k[u] by t(u^n) = 1 if n = 1 and 0 otherwise. So t = T is the element dual to u.
- This is the classical duality between the polynomial coalgebra (Delta u = u⊗1 + 1⊗u) and the divided-power algebra Gamma(T).
- Base change to k' therefore gives A_*(s, s^+, gamma, t)(k') ≅ A_*(k'{{T}}, k'{{T}}^+, gamma, T) ≅ A_*(k')^∧. The completed pd-forms over k' are recovered.

(3) A k-predual. Set A_k^* := A^*(s_k, \bar s_k, gamma_k, t_k). Then A_*(k')^∧ ≅ Hom_k(A_k^*, k') 'with all structures'. So the pd-forms over any k' are the k-linear dual of a single object defined over k.

(4) Bigrading. When s, \bar s and \bar s − s are graded (the ordinary u-grading on k[[u]], matching the ordinary grading on k'{{T}}) and t = T has degree 1, A_k^* carries a bigrading: polynomial degree and form degree.

(5) Application to spaces. Define a chain-level pd de Rham object C_*^{DR,pd}(X, k) := C_*^{DR}(X, k[u], k[u]^+, gamma_k, t_k). Then Hom_k(C_*^{DR,pd}(X, k), k') recovers all known structures, bigrading included, on the pd de Rham cochain complex C^*_{DR,pd}(X, k').

(6) The last line begins a remark that all the C_*^{DR,pd}(X, k) are of some special kind ('relevant'? illegible) and is cut off.

The purpose: a universal 'homological' (chain-level) model over k whose dual gives the pd de Rham cochains over every k', compatible with base change and with the bigrading.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but the page is a sketch. The functors A_* and A^*, and the precise meaning of the quadruple (s, s^+, gamma, t), are defined on earlier pages and cannot be checked here.

There is a notational wobble between k[[u]] (power series) and k[u] (polynomials). The duality Hom_k(-, k') with divided-power series k'{{T}} is clean for the graded or continuous dual. Literally, k[u] dualizes to divided-power series, and k[[u]] dualizes continuously to divided-power polynomials. Grothendieck compensates by completing (the ∧), but the precise topology and finiteness hypotheses are not stated.

ideas.what: Duality between the polynomial coalgebra k[u] and the divided-power algebra in T (t = T dual to u, t(u^n) = δ_{n,1}), used to define coefficients for de Rham-type cochains.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric coalgebra / divided-power algebra duality (Hopf duality Sym ↔ Γ)

ideas.what: Divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices, giving a commutative cochain model over arbitrary rings, with base change k → k'.
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial forms with divided powers / pd de Rham complex of simplicial sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1976 Cartan seminar 'Théories cohomologiques'); B. Cenkl and R. Porter (late 1970s-80s)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished IHES lecture notes, as far as I know

ideas.what: A chain-level (homological) k-predual C_*^{DR,pd}(X, k) such that Hom_k(C_*, k') is the pd de Rham cochain complex over every k' 'with all structures', including a bigrading. The construction is parametrized by abstract 'line data' (s, s^+, gamma, t).
ideas.modern_name: Universal predual / coalgebraic model of pd-forms; parametrized 'interval object' formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; no standard attribution known to me

missed.claim: The de Rham cochain complex is parametrized by abstract coefficient data (s, s^+, gamma, t): a pd 'line' with a coordinate. This suggests building de Rham-type models from other one-dimensional (pd) formal objects than the additive line, with the standard pd-forms as the special case s = k[u]. A single universal chain object over k is defined whose duals give all base changes.
missed.quote: C_*^{DR,ld}(X,k) =df C_*^{DR}(X, k[u], k[u]^+, γ_k^*, t_k) ... il viendra Hom_k(C_*^{DR,ld}(X,k),k') les structures connues (y compris bigraduation)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Cenkl-Porter and Cartan treat pd polynomial forms for the additive line only. A formalism with variable 'line data' and a universal coalgebraic predual could connect to modern work on integral cochain models (e.g. E∞/pd models, Mandell's theorem, Toën's affine stacks). Its significance is uncertain without the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a technically natural use of the Sym/Γ duality to give a predual for divided-power de Rham cochains. Its interest lies in the generality (abstract line data, universal predual, bigrading), which seems unpublished. Related pd-forms work by Cartan and Cenkl-Porter exists, so a specialist would find it plausible rather than startling.
transcription_corrections: 'ld' in C_*^{DR,ld} is most likely 'pd' (puissances divisées), given the subject of the cote.
'k[{T}]' on line 3 is probably the divided-power algebra k{{T}} (or k⟨T⟩), not a polynomial ring.
'syst. de coord. [?] divisées' likely reads 'systèmes de coordonnées divisées canoniques' (canonical divided-power coordinates).
The neighbouring-page transcriptions are of the SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript on the reverse side, not of Grothendieck's handwritten notes.
